title: Senior Platform Automation Engineer
description:
PUBLIC DEMONSTRATION NOTICE
This is a wholly fictional job posting created for an offline public software demonstration. Rivermark Platform Services, this opening, its customers, compensation, benefits, dates, and contact details do not represent a real employer or employment opportunity.

ABOUT RIVERMARK
Rivermark Platform Services is depicted as a remote-first United States software company that builds workflow and infrastructure products for regional logistics providers, field-service networks, and public-interest organizations. Its fictional customers operate distributed systems that must remain understandable during maintenance, incident response, and controlled change. The company is modernizing a shared automation platform used by product engineers and operations teams to provision cloud resources, apply configuration, publish service inventories, and observe scheduled work.

The Platform Foundations group owns common services, reference implementations, release controls, and operational guidance. Application teams retain ownership of their product decisions and production approvals. Rivermark values small reviewable changes, clear interfaces, durable runbooks, and automation that makes authority visible instead of silently expanding it.

ROLE IMPACT
The Senior Platform Automation Engineer will help turn a collection of useful scripts and controller jobs into a dependable internal platform. This person will work across Python services, Ansible and AWX workflows, cloud infrastructure, search, telemetry, and developer experience. The role combines hands-on implementation with operational follow-through: engineers are expected to test what they build, participate in support, explain failure modes, and improve the path from a local change to an approved release.

During the first six months, success means shipping at least one bounded platform capability, improving evidence for scheduled automation, and reducing ambiguity in a recurring support workflow. Success is measured through reliability, adoption, recovery quality, and maintainability rather than through lines of code or the number of automated changes.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Design and maintain Python services, command-line tools, and REST interfaces that coordinate inventory, configuration, and deployment workflows without hiding approval boundaries.
- Improve Ansible roles and AWX job templates used across development, validation, and production environments, including input validation, dry-run behavior, execution evidence, and failure recovery.
- Build and review Terraform modules for AWS and Azure foundations while partnering with security and service owners on access, network, encryption, and retention requirements.
- Develop observability for automation services with OpenSearch, Grafana, Prometheus, structured logs, and service-level indicators that connect alerts to clear operator actions.
- Strengthen scheduled-work reliability by examining queue behavior, concurrency, retries, idempotence, partial failures, and the integrity of downstream inventory records.
- Maintain tested release workflows in GitHub Actions and Jenkins, including packaging, dependency review, changelogs, environment promotion, rollback evidence, and human approval gates.
- Participate in a shared on-call rotation after onboarding, lead blameless follow-up for platform incidents, and convert recurring support work into safer defaults, documentation, or focused backlog items.
- Collaborate with application engineers on reusable patterns while keeping domain-specific policy and final production authority with the teams that own those services.
- Review code and design proposals, mentor engineers through debugging and operational readiness, and contribute concise architecture notes and runbooks.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Seven or more years of software, infrastructure, platform, or reliability engineering experience, including ownership of production-facing automation.
- Strong Python engineering skills with practical experience designing modules or services, writing unit and integration tests, handling failure states, and supporting released code.
- Hands-on experience with Ansible, AWX or a comparable automation controller, and at least one infrastructure-as-code workflow.
- Working knowledge of AWS or Azure, Linux administration, identity and access controls, networking fundamentals, and common service troubleshooting techniques.
- Experience building or operating monitoring, logging, or search systems and using telemetry to guide incident response and reliability improvements.
- Familiarity with version control, peer review, continuous integration, staged delivery, and documented rollback practices.
- Ability to explain technical tradeoffs to engineers and operational partners, produce useful written guidance, and work independently in a distributed team.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Experience developing Kubernetes controllers or operating a GitOps platform with Argo CD or Flux.
- Familiarity with Backstage, Crossplane, OpenTelemetry, service-mesh operations, or comparable internal-platform building blocks.
- Production experience with Go, event-driven services, or high-volume workflow orchestration.
- Experience designing multi-tenant platform controls, usage reporting, or cost-allocation signals.
- Exposure to SOC 2 readiness, supply-chain security, policy-as-code, or evidence collection for regulated services.
- Experience measuring developer adoption and improving platform interfaces based on support trends and user research.

WORKING MODEL AND COLLABORATION
This fictional role is full-time and remote within the United States. The team reserves 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Central Time for planned collaboration while allowing engineers to arrange the rest of their schedule with their manager. The position includes an on-call rotation averaging one week in six after a supported onboarding period and up to four planned travel days each year for team workshops.

Engineers receive access only to the environments needed for their current work. Production changes require peer review, recorded validation, and approval from the accountable service owner. Rivermark expects respectful written communication, accessible documentation, and reasonable handoffs across time zones. Interview exercises use synthetic data and do not require candidates to provide proprietary code from a current or former employer.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
For this fictional demonstration, the annual base-pay range is $148,000 to $184,000 USD. A fictional offer would consider role scope, relevant experience, and the employee's approved work location, and could include a target annual bonus of up to 10 percent. The demo package also describes medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid basic life and disability coverage; a retirement plan with a 4 percent employer match; 20 days of paid time off; 12 company holidays; paid sick time; paid caregiver leave; and a $1,800 annual learning allowance. Remote employees are depicted as receiving a company-managed workstation and a $100 monthly connectivity stipend. These figures and programs are illustrative only and create no commitment or eligibility.

APPLICATION CONTEXT
The fictional review process includes a recruiter conversation, a technical discussion grounded in a synthetic platform scenario, a collaborative system-design session, and a final conversation about working practices. Candidates may request an accessible interview format through talent@rivermark.example.test. Applications for this demonstration close on August 14, 2026, and are never transmitted by the offline demo. Rivermark does not exist, no hiring decision will be made, and no applicant data should be entered into this fixture.
